title: Closed-Loop Reliability application repair
description: A genuine project record managed by the application for the actual existing-application repair job. The project is not the application itself: it is one persisted project inside the application, using the same project model and views as every other project. It preserves the real work and evidence completed through Stage 10 and truthfully stops at Stage 11 because ten genuinely independent execution contexts have not been completed.
nextRequiredAction: Create ten genuinely independent fresh execution contexts from CANDIDATE-001, preserve each output separately, then independently verify every applicable requirement for every run.

userEnteredData.exactRequest: The existing application must be repaired in place. Do not create a second application, replacement application, alternate version, prototype, demo, mock application, or parallel implementation. There must be one application only, containing only the application and components actually required for the intended product.
userEnteredData.requestedDeliverable: The existing Closed-Loop Reliability GitHub Pages application repaired in place as one coherent phone-first human-facing product implementing the complete 30-stage workflow and Appendices A-F semantics, with a genuine fully inspectable project and verified running behavior.
suppliedMaterials: Controlling application-repair instruction supplied by the user
30-stage Mobile Closed-Loop Agent Reliability Workbook specification
constraints: Repair in place with minimal coherent architectural change
No fabricated completion or synthetic independent runs
All substantive project data, prompts, outputs, evidence, defects, blockers, changes, and history remain inspectable

requirements.requirement: Exactly one existing application is repaired in place; no replacement, alternate, prototype, demo, or parallel application exists.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Repository and deployment expose one application entry point and one product UI.
requirements.failureCondition: A second application or alternate product entry point exists.

requirements.requirement: The primary interface is phone-first and human-facing; project state, human actions, blockers, outputs and evidence dominate normal screens rather than implementation bookkeeping.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Rendered phone UI presents compact project-oriented views and contextual actions.
requirements.failureCondition: Normal screens are dominated by developer/agent bookkeeping, giant controls, or raw checklist walls.

requirements.requirement: All 30 workbook stages remain semantically represented with purpose, state, evidence, dependencies, gates, blocking behavior, history and transitions.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: All 30 stages exist in order and their underlying controls and generated instructions remain available.
requirements.failureCondition: Any required stage or semantic control is absent or bypassed.

requirements.requirement: Appendices A-F operate contextually as fresh-context, blocker, change/invalidation, release, new-job and output-receipt capabilities rather than standalone checklist walls.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Each appendix behavior exists as reusable workflow functionality where relevant.
requirements.failureCondition: Appendix semantics are deleted or represented only as disconnected repetitive checklists.

requirements.requirement: Projects preserve and expose user data, sources, research, requirements, tests, generated prompts and instructions, outputs, evidence, runs, comparisons, defects, blockers, changes, regressions, baselines, products, audits, release decisions, hashes and history as applicable.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Project views and history make substantive records inspectable without replacing them with opaque status summaries.
requirements.failureCondition: Substantive records disappear, are inaccessible, or are replaced by summary-only state.

requirements.requirement: The retained test project uses the ordinary project model, persistence and views used by every other project; it is a project inside the application, not the application itself or a mock UI fixture.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Selecting the test project loads ordinary persisted runtime state through the same views and controls.
requirements.failureCondition: The test project uses special display-only UI, hard-coded cards, or a separate application path.

requirements.requirement: The retained project records a genuine job with controlling user authority separated from repository implementation evidence.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Source inventory explicitly distinguishes controlling instructions from implementation evidence.
requirements.failureCondition: Existing code is treated as authority for what the product ought to be.

requirements.requirement: Opening the retained project exposes its original request, supplied material inventory, research, requirements, tests, production instruction, generated prompts, captured outputs, evidence, blockers, changes and stage history through the point actually reached.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Overview, Work, Runs, Issues, Release and History expose the populated records.
requirements.failureCondition: Any substantive populated project class is hidden behind an opaque status or missing from the project.

requirements.requirement: Generated prompts, instructions and captured responses remain inspectable at the relevant stage and in complete project history.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Stage detail and History display exact generated/captured material.
requirements.failureCondition: Generated or captured work is hidden or discarded.

requirements.requirement: UNKNOWN, NONE, NOT APPLICABLE, SATISFIED, VIOLATED, UNDETERMINED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED and BLOCKED remain distinct and missing mandatory evidence cannot become success.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: State vocabulary and release behavior preserve the defined distinctions.
requirements.failureCondition: Missing evidence is converted to success or state meanings are conflated.

requirements.requirement: Material changes preserve history and invalidate stale downstream determinations with required revalidation.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: A material change records its audit entry and invalidates affected downstream completed/ready determinations.
requirements.failureCondition: Stale downstream validation continues to count after an upstream material change.

requirements.requirement: Independent work preserves fresh-context identity, frozen authorized inputs, contamination controls and separate outputs; synthetic independence is prohibited.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Fresh-context records contain frozen versions and explicit contamination controls and runs remain separate.
requirements.failureCondition: Runs share prohibited information or duplicated/synthetic records count as independent execution.

requirements.requirement: Release readiness derives from actual evidence and exact release bytes must match audited bytes when release identity is required.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Release view derives state from evidence and runtime hash comparison prevents authorization on mismatch or blocked gate.
requirements.failureCondition: Release is inferred from absence of defects or mismatched bytes are authorized.

requirements.requirement: New Project starts clean at Stage 01 without inheriting another project's requirements, tests, evidence, blockers, runs, baseline, product, audits or release decision.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Creating a new project produces empty project-specific registries and Stage 01 current state.
requirements.failureCondition: Any prior job-specific workflow evidence is silently inherited.

requirements.requirement: Controls use compact mobile proportions, deliberate hierarchy and progressive disclosure without giant buttons or checklist walls.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: 393x852 rendering shows compact controls and project-oriented hierarchy; detailed controls are opened only when needed.
requirements.failureCondition: Oversized controls, crude layout, or checklist walls dominate the phone interface.

requirementResolution.observedDefect: Implementation evidence could be mistaken for controlling requirement authority.
requirementResolution.resolution: All product requirements trace to the controlling user specification; repository files remain evidentiary only.

tests.procedure: Confirm exactly one root HTML application entry and one deployed application.
Render the application at 393x852 and inspect project hierarchy and control sizing.
Confirm all 30 ordered stages and stage-specific generated instructions exist.
Exercise fresh-context preparation, blocker creation, invalidation, derived release, clean new project and output receipt behavior.
Inspect project model collections and all project-facing views.
Load the retained project through the ordinary registry/state/view path and verify projectData survives conversion.
Inspect source authority records and confirm repository artifacts are evidence only.
Open retained project Overview, Workflow, Work, Runs, Issues, Release and History and inspect populated project records.
Open stage detail and History and inspect exact generated prompt and captured output records.
Verify distinct outcome vocabulary and mandatory blocker/release behavior.
Apply a material upstream change and verify downstream determinations are invalidated and history preserved.
Prepare an independent context and inspect frozen versions and contamination controls.
Verify evidence-derived release state and audited/release SHA-256 identity control.
Create a new project and verify Stage 01 plus empty project-specific registries.
Inspect phone rendering for compact buttons, spacing, hierarchy and progressive disclosure.

mutations.violationMode: Add a second application entry point.
Replace the retained project with a hard-coded display-only project card.
Treat missing mandatory evidence as acceptance.
Count duplicated records as independent runs.

productionInstruction.objective: Repair the existing closed-loop-tracker application in place without creating another application.
sourceAuthority: Repository files are implementation evidence only
productionInstruction.scope: The existing GitHub Pages application only.
procedure: Preserve the single existing application and working workflow engine.
Use one persisted project model for normal projects and the retained project.
Keep all 30 stages and Appendix A-F semantics as contextual application behavior.
Keep user data, research, requirements, tests, prompts, outputs, evidence, defects, blockers, changes and history inspectable.
Keep controls compact and phone-first and move technical detail behind contextual disclosure.
Preserve blockers, invalidation, fresh-context preparation, output receipts, convergence/baseline/product/audit records, evidence traceability and release-byte controls.
Verify source, exact deployed bytes, phone rendering and live controls before claiming completion.
productionInstruction.failureBehavior: Missing mandatory evidence remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED. Never fabricate independent runs, verification, baseline approval, product acceptance, or release identity.
productionInstruction.completionCriteria: Every mandatory application requirement has affirmative implementation and verification evidence and the deployed application passes required source, render and live-interaction checks.

defects.rootCause: Control sizing was not constrained to ordinary phone interface proportions.
defects.correction: Use compact 30-34px primary controls, tighter spacing and progressive disclosure.
